title: Complex magnetic properties of EuAgAs single crystals
authors: Karolina Kowalczyk, Kamila Komędera, Janusz Przewoźnik, Łukasz Gondek, Czesław Kapusta, Wojciech Tabiś, Michał Babij, Lan Maria Tran, Damian Rybicki
abstract: EuAgAs is an antiferromagnetic topological material exhibiting intriguing magnetic behavior. We investigate its structural, magnetic, and local electronic properties using X ray diffraction, Mössbauer spectroscopy, dc magnetization, ac susceptibility, and heat capacity measurements. The results confirm antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_\text{N}$ and reveal pronounced magnetic anisotropy and several field induced metamagnetic transitions. We construct the magnetic phase diagram of EuAgAs, identifying several distinct magnetic regions. The field and temperature dependent behavior observed suggests a noncollinear magnetic structure in the low field regime. The sequence of field induced transitions resembles that observed in centrosymmetric rare earth compounds hosting skyrmion phases, suggesting that competing magnetic interactions may play an important role in stabilizing the observed magnetic states.
summary: This work experimentally characterizes the complex magnetic phase diagram of EuAgAs, an antiferromagnetic topological material. Using multiple techniques including magnetometry and heat capacity, the authors confirm antiferromagnetic ordering and reveal several field-induced transitions. The results strongly suggest a noncollinear magnetic structure, making it a valuable system for studying competing magnetic interactions.
main_problem: To thoroughly investigate the structural, magnetic, and local electronic properties of the antiferromagnetic topological material EuAgAs single crystals, clarifying its complex magnetic behavior.
main_result: The material exhibits antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx 12$ K, characterized by pronounced magnetic anisotropy and multiple field-induced metamagnetic transitions, suggesting a noncollinear or potentially skyrmion-like magnetic ground state.
method: A combination of experimental techniques was used, including X-ray diffraction, heat capacity measurements, DC/AC magnetization measurements, and Mössbauer spectroscopy on Eu isotopes.
model_or_system: The study focuses on EuAgAs, a hexagonal crystal structure ($P6_3/mmc$) rare-earth compound whose magnetic properties are governed by competing magnetic interactions, possibly described by RKKY-type interactions.
key_observables: Magnetic susceptibility ($\chi'$ and $\chi''$), heat capacity ($C_p$), lattice parameters ($a, c$), Mössbauer isomer shift ($\delta$), and magnetization ($M$) as a function of temperature and applied magnetic field.
important_parameters: Antiferromagnetic ordering temperature ($T_N \approx 12$ K); effective magnetic moments ($\mu_{\perp c}^{	ext{eff}} \approx 7.24 \mu_B$); Weiss temperature constants ($	heta_{\perp c}^p = 12.16 	ext{ K}$); and critical magnetic fields inducing transitions.
main_assumptions: The analysis sometimes approximates $C_p$ by neglecting the electronic contribution, and the identification of exotic phases like skyrmions is based on analogy with other systems, lacking direct confirmation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate XRD results showing lattice parameter changes, heat capacity curves revealing the $T_N$ peak, and magnetic phase diagrams mapping out transitions based on susceptibility and magnetization measurements.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the structure (XRD), thermal properties ($C_p$), and magnetic response (M, $\chi$, Mössbauer) of EuAgAs. It builds a magnetic phase diagram by correlating anomalies in these measurements to identify the magnetic ground state and field-induced transitions.
why_interesting: The investigation into field-induced metamagnetic transitions and the suggestion of noncollinear or skyrmion-like states in a real material provides an excellent experimental benchmark for theoretical models of frustrated magnetism and competing exchange interactions.
